clue.text: Steer one vehicle up before the entrance/

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces before it are read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Advice to a driver: turn the car round before pulling in at the gateway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns both pieces together, as written upward in a down light; 'the' is a link and the stray slash is a printing mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer a ship or vehicle is to direct its course, a synonym.

clue.text: Is it nothing to the capital of Egypt? Yes and no

definitions.text: Is it nothing to the capital of Egypt? Yes and no

indicators.note: capital here means the first, upper-case letter of the word Egypt

explanation.surface: A teasing question about whether some feature matters to the Egyptian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Yes: the river is literally 'nothing' plus E; no: the great river is everything to Egypt, so the whole clue both builds and describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river running through Egypt is the country's lifeline, the opposite of nothing to it.

clue.text: Close attention given to British in US city

indicators.note: in tells us the attention and British pieces sit inside the city letters

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Careful attention paid to a Briton visiting an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' is an adjective meaning near at hand, not the verb to shut; 'given to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close is near at hand, a synonym.

clue.text: Unease at flicks turning into disgust

indicators.note: the letters flick about and turn over, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A feeling of unease watching films that becomes outright revulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flicks' looks like cinema films, but with 'turning' it signals the anagram of UNEASE AT; 'into' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To disgust someone is to sicken them, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Mark all but penning various lives in a form of fiction

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so one piece goes inside the other
all but means the word is used without its final letter

parts.note: to mark something is to notice it

indicators.note: various means the letters come in assorted order

explanation.surface: Someone noting how different lives are told as a sort of story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but' drops the last letter of the synonym for Mark; 'penning' puts the 'various' anagram inside it, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Novelistic describes writing in the manner of long prose fiction.

clue.text: Some gardener in Ealing producing the Guernsey lily

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A London gardener grows a particular flower in their plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerine sarniensis is the botanical name of the Guernsey lily, a South African bulb.

clue.text: Caution Spanish girl taking part in fighting

indicators.note: taking part in places the girl inside the fighting

parts.note: Ines is a Spanish girl's name

explanation.surface: A Spanish woman is warned to be careful about joining a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Wariness is care in the face of danger, a synonym of caution.

clue.text: Seat positioned on part of golf-course

parts.note: the tee is where each hole is started

explanation.surface: A bench placed beside one of the starting areas on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee is a sofa, a long upholstered seat.

clue.text: An extreme, say, recalled in a US writer

indicators.note: in puts the turned letters inside the writer's name

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: A remark about an American author recollecting some extreme example.
explanation.definitionFit: An apogee is the highest point or climax, an extreme.

clue.text: Current supplier's w-wrath

parts.note: the stammered first letter of the next word supplies a W

explanation.surface: An electricity company's stammering fury.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in 'w-wrath' gives a spare W before IRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire carries electric current to where it is needed.

clue.text: Resistor blown? That is doing for kitchen device

indicators.note: a blown component is wrecked, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An electrical resistor has burnt out, finishing off some kitchen gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing for' is a link; the anagram of RESISTOR gives ROTISSER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotisserie is a cooking appliance that turns meat on a spit.

clue.text: Weak seabird losing tail in road

indicators.note: in places the shortened bird inside the road
losing tail means the word drops its last letter

explanation.surface: A feeble seabird with no tail feathers wanders into the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing tail' trims the bird's last letter before it goes inside the road; 'Weak' as in a diluted drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Watery drinks are thin and diluted, so weak.

clue.text: Flap when dirty character's found in vandalised toilets

indicators.note: found in puts the dirty character inside the other letters
vandalised means smashed up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a pig is a dirty person

explanation.surface: Panic when a filthy lout is caught in some wrecked public lavatories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flap' looks like a panic but is the defining noun; 'found in' puts the dirty character inside the 'vandalised' anagram; 'when' and the ''s' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The epiglottis is the flap of cartilage that covers the windpipe when swallowing.

clue.text: One who's tested a bomb in a river

indicators.note: in puts the letters for a bomb inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

explanation.surface: Someone under scrutiny over a bomb found in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in south-west England; the second 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An examinee is a candidate sitting an exam, someone being tested.

clue.text: Went out hot, not cold

indicators.note: not means the following letter is left out

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone who left warm rather than chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: To have exited is to have left or departed.

clue.text: Desires to forgo first salary?

indicators.note: forgo first means the word gives up its opening letter

explanation.surface: A question whether ambitions should be sacrificed for pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; the question mark marks salary as an example of the defined word.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are income from work, and a salary is one kind.

clue.text: Hurried round about most of article's profound parts

indicators.note: about means surrounding the other piece
round turns the word back on itself
most of means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone rushing around most of a story's deeper passages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns the hurried word backwards, and 'about' wraps it round the shortened article ('most of'); 'Hurried round' reads as a phrase but splits in two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: The depths are the deepest, most profound places or parts.

clue.text: Feeling united, investing in Japanese and French currencies

parts.note: the sen is a small Japanese currency unit

indicators.note: investing means clothing or wrapping, so the letter goes in among the coins

explanation.surface: A sense of unity among investors in the yen and the franc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing in' puts the letter for united among the coins; 'and' is a link, and 'currencies' applies to both the Japanese and French units.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensuous means appealing to the senses, so relating to physical feeling.

clue.text: Loose upper garment to reveal trunk (or needs doing up)

parts.note: a bole is a tree trunk

indicators.note: in a down clue, doing up means writing the word upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: Instructions to show off a chest, unless it needs fastening first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reveal' and 'needs' are links; 'trunk' looks like a body but is a tree's.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolero is a short open jacket worn over other clothes.

clue.text: Australian native rejected exam regulation, getting nothing

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the pair is read backwards

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: An Aboriginal Australian turned down an exam rule and was left with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses ORAL and LAW together to give WALLARO; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallaroo is a kangaroo species native to Australia.

clue.text: Hunk's activity: a rise in naughtiness!

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise means the word is written upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: A muscleman's hobby is causing a surge in bad behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: The ''s' after Hunk is a link (is); 'a rise' reads the naughtiness word upward. Adonis was the beautiful youth of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: An Adonis is a strikingly handsome young man, after the youth in Greek myth.

clue.text: Mysterious Pole tailing a king

indicators.note: tailing means following behind, so this piece comes after

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A Polish man following a monarch around for unclear reasons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but means a rod, CANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcane means secret, understood by few, so mysterious.

clue.text: Useful things, hunting dogs, heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A pack of hounds sets off, a handy thing to have.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are valuable or useful possessions.

clue.text: Mill owners with this merit?

parts.note: millionaires, owners of a mill or more, have this quality of being worth a lot; read straight, it is deservingness

explanation.surface: Asking whether factory owners deserve their standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mill' looks like a factory but is short for a million: the very rich have a big net worth.
explanation.definitionFit: Worthiness is merit, the quality of deserving respect.

clue.text: Sportsman who's up and down

explanation.surface: An athlete whose mood swings between high and low.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is an Oxford or Cambridge student who has represented the university at sport; 'up' means in residence at university.
explanation.definitionFit: A university sports representative is awarded this colour; and feeling low or sad is the same colour word.

clue.text: Prevents groups cutting discs initially

indicators.note: cutting here means removing, so a letter is cut out
initially points at the first letter of the word discs

explanation.surface: Groups stop recording discs at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' removes the D, the first letter of 'discs', from BANDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To ban something is to prohibit or prevent it.

clue.text: Handing out booze, one hears the sound of complaints?

indicators.note: one hears means the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

explanation.surface: A drinks server overhears grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the sound of' is a link; to wine someone is to ply them with wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Wining means serving wine to guests, giving them drink.

clue.text: Love's language involving kiss and flesh

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the kiss sits within

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
X is a kiss, as at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Romance as a language of kisses and bodies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flesh' is meat here; 'and' is a link, and X goes between O and TONGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ox tongue is a cut of meat, flesh sold for eating.
